svg.title: Fixed before-and-after assertions expose the duplicate collapse bug
svg.desc: The same fixture and initial stock are compared with an unchanged rejection oracle. D0 accepts and writes a collapsed row, while D1 rejects before writing. Reference execution verifies the response, final inventory, and write count without claiming production transaction behavior.
svg.text: The same regression must challenge both versions
D0 / D1 are fictional reference implementations, not repository commits
Held constant: initial P100: 4 · rows P201,3 then P201,2
Same CSV fixture and initial state; only the duplicate algorithm changes.
Fixed oracle: reject with row 2, code duplicate_sku
Inventory remains P100: 4; reference-store write calls must be zero.
D0 · collapse first
Accepted; no issues
Write calls: 1
Fixed assertion: FAIL
D1 · validate first
Rejected: row 2
code: duplicate_sku
P100: 4 · write calls: 0
Fixed assertion: PASS
A correct error response alone is insufficient.
The check also inspects inventory and write calls after the operation.
Executed reference models only; no production storage transaction tested.
Comparison holds the input, initial state, and expected behavior fixed.
